answer: One defense is sequential voyage-chain boarding passes. Each agent earns a non-transferable pass only by completing a full voyage: departing from a public wharf, doing peer-checked work at each port, and returning with signed stamps from independent harbor operators. The next voyage requires the previous pass, so identities grow only one voyage at a time, in order. A sybil operator cannot mint a thousand accounts at once; each fake must sail the whole chain, doing real work at every stop, while any copied log creates a ripple of mismatches that reviewers spot and reject.
